detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Qwen3-30B-A3B GB200 MXFP8 performance preset runs out of memory in the first optimizer step after full-iteration CUDA-graph capture on newer framework stacks, as reported in [#6307](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/issues/6307). Switch `qwen3_30b_a3b_pretrain_8gpu_gb200_fp8mx_config` to Transformer Engine graphs scoped to `attn`, `moe_router`, and `moe_preprocess`.

Keep the existing benchmark helper so that HybridEP, expert communication overlap, delayed weight-gradient computation, paged stash, expert padding, capacity, and allocator settings match the successful diagnostic. The only runtime changes are `cuda_graph_impl` and `cuda_graph_scope`. Update the existing recipe regression test to check the new graph settings while retaining its checks for precision, topology, batches, environment, and benchmark behavior.

This mitigates the preset failure. The underlying full-iteration memory regression and the hang after an OOM remain tracked by #6307. The related [#5356](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/5356) changed the B200 preset; this change applies to GB200.

## Validation

Completed GPU experiments:

| Experiment | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Graph settings only | All eight ranks completed 30 iterations with graph replay, finite losses, and zero skipped/NaN steps. Graph pool: 33.684 GiB; post-capture peak allocated: 138.083 GiB; peak reserved: about 174.1 GiB. Mean step time over iterations 16–30: 8,450.6 ms. |
| Partial graphs plus companion settings | Also completed 30 iterations. Changing allocator/record-stream settings and disabling paged stash/expert padding provided no memory-headroom benefit; mean step time was 8,819 ms. Those changes are excluded. |

The graph-only experiment used 8 GB200 GPUs across two nodes, MBS 4, GBS 512, sequence length 4096, EP8, HybridEP, and MXFP8.

## Performance and remaining validation

The diagnostic still reached approximately 184.29 of 184.31 GiB device memory and emitted allocator OOM-retry warnings before capture, so the successful 30-step run does not establish comfortable memory headroom or long-run stability.

The model verification card's historical full-iteration result is about 6.50 seconds per step, versus 8.45 seconds for this partial-graph diagnostic. These measurements use different stacks and timing windows; they are not a matched estimate of the graph-mode performance cost. The card remains an explicitly pinned historical result. 

Related to #6307.

detail.title: fix(recipe): use partial CUDA graphs for Qwen3 GB200 MXFP8

files.patch:
@@ -310,8 +310,11 @@ def qwen3_30b_a3b_pretrain_8gpu_gb200_fp8mx_config() -> ConfigContainer:
 
     _benchmark_common(cfg)
 
-    # Full-iteration graphs remain benchmark-only because they alter natural-routing auxiliary loss.
+    # Preserve the tuned HybridEP, paged-stash, and overlap settings from the benchmark helper.
     _enable_hybridep_full_iteration_mxfp8(cfg)
+    # Full-iteration capture OOMs at the optimizer step on newer stacks (issue #6307).
+    cfg.model.cuda_graph_impl = "transformer_engine"
+    cfg.model.cuda_graph_scope = ["attn", "moe_router", "moe_preprocess"]
     cfg.model.recompute_modules = []
     # Keep process settings next to the recipe so users can see the exact benchmark environment.
     cfg.env_vars = {

@@ -836,12 +836,11 @@ def test_qwen3_30b_a3b_gb200_fp8mx_perf_recipe_uses_main_recipe(
     assert perf_cfg.model.recompute_granularity is None
     assert perf_cfg.model.recompute_modules == []
 
-    # Full-iteration graphs conflict with the main recipe's loss-NaN check and
-    # therefore remain benchmark-only.
+    # Partial graphs avoid the GB200 full-iteration OOM; the benchmark also captures attention.
     assert main_cfg.model.cuda_graph_impl == "transformer_engine"
     assert main_cfg.model.cuda_graph_scope == ["moe_router", "moe_preprocess"]
-    assert perf_cfg.model.cuda_graph_impl == "full_iteration"
-    assert perf_cfg.model.cuda_graph_scope == []
+    assert perf_cfg.model.cuda_graph_impl == "transformer_engine"
+    assert perf_cfg.model.cuda_graph_scope == ["attn", "moe_router", "moe_preprocess"]
 
 
 def test_qwen3_235b_a22b_lora_defaults(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):

> @janbernloehr which container did you use to validate this? I think this OOM was resolved with a TE upgrade to TE 2.20.

The validation used TE `2.20.2+6ea2a74a`, PyTorch `2.15.0a0+875d815502`, CUDA 13.5, Megatron-Bridge c0e164e, and MCore a0f793d.

I also checked the latest runs from October 7–9. All three already use TE 2.20.2 and still OOM with cuda_graph_impl=full_iteration in DistributedOptimizer.copy_group_grads after two completed iterations. The failing runs hold 101.02 GiB in CUDA-graph private pools, so the TE upgrade has not resolved this particular workload’s OOM.

With TE-scoped graphs on attn, moe_router, and moe_preprocess, all eight ranks completed 30 iterations with finite losses and no skipped/NaN steps; the graph pool dropped to 33.684 GiB. That validation used CLI overrides on the earlier Bridge revision above. The exact PR commit still needs GPU validation.
